Work / Premium Positioning System / Umiya Sushi
Restaurant · Repositioning

Umiya Sushi.

From a coupon-menu template to Las Vegas' favorite all-you-can-eat sushi.

Umiya's original site was a stock GoDaddy template — a Fjalla One headline dumping four AYCE prices onto a stock photo, no real hierarchy, no story, nothing that said "premium." The repositioning keeps the same core offer (unlimited, made-to-order sushi) and reframes it as a destination: fresh fish daily, a real menu, real reviews, real atmosphere.

Role
Brand Reposition · UI Redesign
Industry
Restaurant · AYCE Sushi
Scope
Full Site Rebuild

Concept & Intent.

The old site sold four prices. Nothing else. No sense of the fish, the chefs, the room, or why anyone should choose Umiya over the sushi place next door.

The redesign leads with the food itself — sashimi, signature rolls, the ritual of the counter — then earns the AYCE pricing as a bonus, not the whole pitch. Trust signals (4.5★, 2,700+ reviews, "never a buffet") do the convincing a template can't.

Before & After
Before GoDaddy Website Builder
  • Hero is a plain photo-plus-price-list split — no headline, no hook, no story
  • Generic bordered logo box, default red button styling, no visual identity
  • Zero social proof — no reviews, ratings, or reason to trust the kitchen
  • Menu, gallery, reservations, and location all missing from the page entirely
After Custom Build
  • Editorial headline + trust bar (4.5★ · 2,700+ reviews · 200+ items) above the fold
  • Full story section, a "Why Umiya" grid, and 9 organized menu categories with real photography
  • Live reservation form, Google Maps location card, and a full photo gallery
  • AYCE reframed as 4 considered tiers ($28–$46), not a wall of raw numbers
